title: The Flagellation of Christ
source: Galleria Nazionale delle Marche, Palazzo Ducale, Urbino (public domain). Full resolution from Wikimedia Commons: Piero della Francesca Flagellazione-gndm-full.jpg (3470 x 2440 px)
caption: Something terrible happens in this painting, and the three men in front don't even look. Who are they? 500 years later, nobody knows for sure. #mystery #perspective #pierodellafrancesca #arthistory #didyouknow
_verify: VERIFIED, Wikipedia EN (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellation_of_Christ_(Piero_della_Francesca)): tempera on panel, 67.5 x 91 cm (some sources say oil and tempera), Galleria Nazionale delle Marche, Urbino; dated 1459-1460 there. Wikipedia IT (it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellazione_di_Cristo_(Piero_della_Francesca)): dating ranges 1444 (Longhi) to 1472 (Battisti), most scholars 1458-1459. Slides say 'Around 1460'.

VERIFIED, Wikipedia EN: the biblical event takes place in an open gallery in the middle distance; the seated man on the left is 'in one sense certainly Pontius Pilate'; signed under the seated figure 'OPVS PETRI DE BVRGO S[AN]C[T]I SEPVLCRI' (not used); a classical figure atop the column behind Christ. Smarthistory (smarthistory.org/?p=1542): golden statue; Pilate ordered Christ flogged; three men dominate the foreground, identities disputed. artrkl.com: the three foreground men are larger in scale than the sacred figures.

VISUAL, not sourced in text: the man in a turban seen from behind (Lavin reads the interior scene as Pilate showing Herod 'with his back turned', Wikipedia EN). Slide 4 only describes what is visible.

THEORY, flagged on slides ('One old theory', 'Another theory', 'A third'): (1) Oddantonio da Montefeltro between his counsellors Manfredo dei Pio and Tommaso dell'Agnello (Wikipedia EN, 'conventional Urbino view'); Oddantonio, first Duke of Urbino, was killed with both counsellors on the night of 21-22 July 1444, aged about 16 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oddantonio_da_Montefeltro). (2) Ginzburg / Ronchey: from left, Cardinal Bessarion, Thomas Palaiologos, Niccolò III d'Este; linked to Byzantium, crusades and the Council of Mantua 1459 (Wikipedia EN + IT). (3) Past, present and future / three ages of man (Marinazzo, Wikipedia EN + IT). Other theories not used: Lavin (Ludovico Gonzaga, Ottaviano Ubaldini), King (Regiomontanus), Gombrich, Pope-Hennessy (Dream of St Jerome).

VERIFIED, perspective: Wikipedia IT says scholars reconstructed the floor in plan and calculated the ideal distance of the viewer's eye; module 4.699 cm (Kenneth Clark), painting 7 x 10 modules. Classic study: R. Wittkower and B.A.R. Carter, 'The perspective of Piero della Francesca's Flagellation', Journal of the Warburg and Courtauld Institutes 16 (1953), pp. 292-302 (philarchive.org/rec/WITTPO). Piero wrote De prospectiva pingendi (Smarthistory, Wikipedia IT).

VERIFIED, theft: Wikipedia IT: stolen from the Palazzo Ducale in Urbino on 6 February 1975 together with the Madonna di Senigallia; both recovered in Locarno, Switzerland, on 22 March 1976. Finestre sull'Arte (finestresullarte.info, Madonna of Senigallia article): stolen night of 5-6 February 1975 with the Flagellation and Raphael's La Muta, recovered the following year in Locarno. Slide 9 says 'a year later in Switzerland'.
NOTE: the 'Convenerunt in unum' frame inscription (lost, reported) is not used.

slides.headline: Something terrible happens here. Nobody looks.
slides.sub: Piero della Francesca, The Flagellation of Christ, c. 1460

slides.headline: Around 1460
slides.text: Around 1460, Piero della Francesca paints the Flagellation of Christ. But the scene in the title is not where you'd expect it.

slides.headline: Pushed to the back
slides.text: Look deep into the hall: Christ, tiny, tied to a column under a golden statue. Calm, almost still, while the whip is raised.

slides.headline: The judge watches
slides.text: On the left sits Pilate, who ordered it, watching. A man in a turban stands with his back to us. But step outside…

slides.headline: Three men, looking away
slides.text: In the sunlit foreground, three men, far bigger than Christ, stand calmly and ignore what happens behind them. Who are they? Nobody knows.

slides.headline: A murdered young duke?
slides.text: One old theory: the barefoot youth is Oddantonio, Urbino's first duke, murdered in 1444 at about 16, beside the two advisers killed with him.

slides.headline: Or a call to crusade?
slides.text: Another theory: Cardinal Bessarion, urging a crusade after Constantinople fell in 1453. A third: past, present, future. Meanwhile, the floor hides mathematics.

slides.headline: A floor you can rebuild
slides.text: Piero wrote a whole treatise on perspective. Scholars have redrawn the floor plan from these tiles, and even calculated where your eye should be.

slides.headline: Stolen, then found
slides.text: In 1975 thieves stole it from Urbino's palace; it was found in Switzerland a year later. Who do you think the three men are?
